chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them:
Regarding a man who became junub during travel while he had water only enough for wudu (ablution), he said: "He performs tayammum and does not perform wudu (ablution)."

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel; the circumstance in which this ruling is being discussed
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: perform tayammum as a substitute purification

ai.seo_question: What should a junub traveler do if he only has enough water for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a traveler who becomes junub and possesses only a small amount of water, enough merely for wudu (ablution). The ruling is that he should perform tayammum instead of using that insufficient water for wudu (ablution), indicating that tayammum applies when water is not sufficient for the required state of taharah.
